user.title: Daylight Engine
user.description: Add lights afterwards with “Add light”; adjust the daylight curve under “Configure”.

abort.single_instance_allowed: Daylight Engine is already set up.

init.title: Daylight curve
init.description: These values apply to all lights; each light's calibration translates them.

data_description.morning_shape: 1 = even, higher = stays near the night value longer, lower = reaches day value earlier
data_description.evening_shape: 1 = even, higher = stays near the night value longer, lower = reaches day value earlier
data_description.morning_low: Degrees above (+) or below (−) the horizon
data_description.evening_low: Degrees above (+) or below (−) the horizon

bright.name: Full brightness
bright.description: Mode e.g. for searching: all lights bright and neutral.

data.turn_on: Switch on lights that are off

data_description.turn_on: When the mode ends, exactly these lights are switched off again.

data_description.min_brightness_change: Smaller changes are not sent, which keeps Zigbee traffic low.
data_description.turn_on_transition: 0 = correct immediately when a light was switched on outside Home Assistant.

error.invalid_curve: Invalid curve: start elevation must be below end elevation and values in range.

data_description.lights: Only group lights that share the same settings. Calibration is still per light.

data_description.transition_mode: Automatic = only if the light reports transition support. Many Wi-Fi lights jump anyway – choose 'never' then.
data_description.detect_manual: If someone changes brightness or colour, the light pauses until it is switched off/on.
data_description.proxy: Also creates “<name> Daylight”: switches on without flashing, and its brightness slider uses the calibration. Use it in dashboards and automations instead of the original light.
